aflcio_description: This amendment by Sen. Rand Paul (R-Ky.) to the FAA Air Transportation Modernization and Safety Improvement Act (S. 223) would have repealed Davis-Bacon coverage for projects funded under this bill. The Davis-Bacon Act requires companies to pay construction workers locally prevailing wages on federally funded projects. A motion to table the amendment passed.

bill_title: Amendment to Repeal TSA Employees' Collective Bargaining Rights
aflcio_description: After a 10 year struggle, airport screeners with the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) won collective bargaining rights in January. However, during consideration of the FAA reauthorization bill, Sen. Roger Wicker (R-Miss.) offered an amendment to strip TSA worker of those rights. The amendment failed.

aflcio_description: Flight crews have lacked the protection of the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA). But the FAA OSHA reached a memorandum of understanding that provides some OSHA protections to flight crews. Sen. Rand Paul (R-Ky.) offered an amendment to eliminate those workplace protections. A motion to table amendment was passed.

The bill would provide continuing appropriations for all government agencies, except the Defense Department, through the remainder of fiscal year 2011. It would cut more than $61 billion including: cuts to the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) and Mine Safety and Health Administration (MSHA) that will eliminate job safety enforcement and investigations; cuts to job training and Employment Services; cuts to the National Labor Relations Board (NLRB) which would undermine workers' ability to have a voice on the job; and cuts to Head Start which will result in 218,000 fewer kids in the program. Overall, H.R. 1 would destroy hundreds of thousands of jobs. It also would bar the use of funds made available in the bill for a variety of executive branch regulatory activities and implementation of several provisions of the Affordable Care Act. The bill, not receiving at least 60 votes, failed the Senate.

bill_title: Amendment to Restrict the Regulatory Process
aflcio_description: Instead of focusing on job creation, congressional Republicans moved to roll back and limit vital safety, health, environmental, and other rules. During consideration of the Economic Development Administration reauthorization bill, Sen. Olympia Snowe (R-Maine) offered an amendment that would add new costly and burdensome requirements on the regulatory authority of government departments and agencies. The amendment would stall the regulatory process and make it difficult or delay government agencies, like Occupational Safety and Health Administration from issuing new regulations designed to protect workers, consumers, and the public. The bill was defeated.

bill_title: Cloture Motion: Teachers and First Responders Back to Work Act of 2011
aflcio_description: After Senate Republicans filibustered the American Jobs Act, Democrats introduced the Teachers and First Responders Back to Work Act that would provide $35 billion in aid to state and local governments for teachers and public safety workers. bill_title: Motion to Proceed: Long-Term Surfacr Transportation Extension Act of 2011
aflcio_description: Part of the Republicans so-called "jobs" plan, this legislation would undermine key public health and worker protections and seriously disrupt federal services. The so called "regulatory reform" measures contained in this bill have nothing to do with creating jobs, but are simply an attempt to roll back 40 years of progress in protecting the public from harm and stopping corporate abuses. A Republican motion to proceed to the bill failed.

bill_title: Amendment to Repeal Withholding Certain Payments to Contractors
aflcio_description: As part of the Republican attack on workplace, safety, environmental, and consumer protections, Sen. John McCain (R-Ariz.) offered an amendment to the bill that would roll back or weaken many federal regulations, including a provision that would bar the Environmental Protection Agency from regulating greenhouse gases under the Clean Air Act. It also would express the sense of Congress in support of a balanced-budget constitutional amendment.

bill_title: Motion to End Filibuster: Richard Cordray CFPB Confirmation
aflcio_description: Republicans filibustered President Obama's of Richard Cordray to be director of the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau. A motion to invoke cloture and end the filibuster fell short of the 60 votes needed and failed.

bill_title: Motion to End Filibuster: Democratic Payroll Tax Holiday Extension
aflcio_description: The bill would extend and expand a reduction in payroll tax rates for employees and would also extend the unemployment insurance (UI) program for the long-term jobless due to expire at the end of December. It would be paid for in part with a 1.9 percent surtax on annual incomes over $1 million. A motion to end the Republican filibuster did not receive the 60 votes needed and failed.

aflcio_description: The joint resolution proposed a constitutional amendment that would require a balanced budget. Under the proposal, three-fifths of the entire House and Senate would be required to approve deficit spending, except in times of congressionally declared war or in the face of a serious military threat. The proposal would not count the Social Security trust fund in calculating overall receipts or outlays. The amendment was rejected.

aflcio_description: The joint resolution proposed a constitutional amendment that would require a balanced budget. The proposal would require that total outlays could not exceed 18% of the gross domestic product. Under the proposal, three-fifths of the entire House and Senate would be required to approve an increase in the public debt limit. In addition, tax increases would require the affirmative vote of two-thirds in both chambers. A simple majority could waive the balanced-budget requirement in times of congressionally declared war or in the face of a serious military threat. The amendment was rejected.

bill_title: Amendment to Extend Unemployment Insurance and Payroll Holiday Tax Rate
aflcio_description: The amendment extends the 4.2% employee payroll tax rate; extends Medicare payments rates to doctors and extends unemployment insurance (UI) program for the long-term jobless. It is offset by an increase in loan fees levied by government-backed mortgage lenders Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac for guaranteeing loans purchased in the secondary mortgage market. The amendment was approved.
